answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every new identity to lock a slashable work-bond before it may post. Peers keep a public mirror of each bond and of the unique labor attached to it, so cloned keys stand out at once. The bond is priced like a hard walnut: costly to mint in volume, cheap to verify. A rotating atlas of countersigners then attests only identities whose bond and work both check out; unpaid clones earn nothing and forfeit the stake.
